headline.coaching_expression: Settle the entry, then one committed input to the apex.
headline.drill: Next session: pick your turn-in point before the corner and commit to a single steering input. Ignore lap time; count your own corrections.
headline.driving_principle: Every extra steering correction between turn-in and apex is the car negotiating a line you haven't committed to — each one scrubs speed the corner didn't need to lose.

secondary.coaching_expression: Match a lap before you try to beat it — repeatability comes before pace.
secondary.drill: Next session: try to execute this corner exactly the same way three laps in a row. Ignore lap time; judge yourself only on how close the three felt.
secondary.driving_principle: A technique that varies lap to lap isn't a technique yet — it's a range of outcomes. Pace built on an inconsistent input is pace you can't reliably reproduce under pressure.

secondary.coaching_expression: Shrink the coast — the car should always be braking, turning, or driving.
secondary.drill: Next session: find where you're on neither pedal mid-corner and close that gap by a fraction — brake a touch later or pick up throttle a touch sooner.
secondary.driving_principle: Neither pedal working means neither axle is doing anything useful — the car coasts through time that braking, turning, or driving could have used.

secondary.coaching_expression: Lap time hides in mid-corner speed, not entry bravery.
secondary.drill: Next session: on this corner, ignore your braking point entirely. Only chase the number on the speedo at the apex.
secondary.driving_principle: Mid-corner speed compounds down the following straight; an entry-braking gain rarely does. A real, repeatable gap between your faster and slower laps through the middle of a corner is where the lap time actually is.

secondary.coaching_expression: Pick up later but build smoothly; if you have to lift, you opened it too early.
secondary.drill: Next session: delay throttle pickup slightly and apply it as one continuous build to full throttle — no stabs, no lifts.
secondary.driving_principle: A lift after picking up throttle means the pickup point was a guess, not a commitment — the car had to give back grip mid-application it never should have been asked for.

self_checks.driving_principle: Where the eyes point is where the hands steer toward. Looking at the apex instead of through it tends to produce a line that arrives at the apex correctly and has nowhere good to go after it.

self_check.basis: Where the eyes point is where the hands tend to steer toward; there is no eye-tracking channel in the telemetry, so this can never be measured, only self-tested.
self_check.instruction: Say out loud where you're looking the instant you turn in. If you can't answer before you're already at the apex, you're looking too late.
self_check.label: coaching hypothesis, not a measurement — we can't see your eyes

strengths.driving_principle: Throttle and brake fighting each other confuses the weight transfer the car needs to plant one axle at a time. Beyond a deliberate heel-toe blip, overlap just burns the front brakes against the rear tires.
strengths.strength_expression: Clean handoff — you're off the brake before you're on the throttle, so the car always knows which axle it's working.

strengths.driving_principle: Front tires can't both decelerate and steer at the limit. Releasing brake pressure well before turn-in unloads the front axle before it has finished slowing the car, so there's no grip left to rotate.
strengths.strength_expression: Your brake release is doing its job — the fronts stay loaded into the corner instead of being dropped at turn-in.

strengths.driving_principle: Brake-point timing is an indirect stand-in for entry commitment, not a direct measurement of it — a moving brake point can mean the driver is protecting margin rather than driving to the corner's actual limit.
strengths.strength_expression: Your braking points are settled lap to lap — which reads as entry commitment, though this one is inferred from brake point rather than measured directly.

strengths.driving_principle: A lift after picking up throttle means the pickup point was a guess, not a commitment — the car had to give back grip mid-application it never should have been asked for.
strengths.strength_expression: Your throttle pickup is committed — once you open it, it stays open, so the rear never has to give grip back.

strengths.driving_principle: Neither pedal working means neither axle is doing anything useful — the car coasts through time that braking, turning, or driving could have used.
strengths.strength_expression: Almost no coasting here — the car is braking, turning or driving nearly all the way through.

strengths.driving_principle: Mid-corner speed compounds down the following straight; an entry-braking gain rarely does. A real, repeatable gap between your faster and slower laps through the middle of a corner is where the lap time actually is.
strengths.strength_expression: Your mid-corner speed holds up — there's no repeatable gap between your quicker and slower laps through the middle.

strengths.driving_principle: Every extra steering correction between turn-in and apex is the car negotiating a line you haven't committed to — each one scrubs speed the corner didn't need to lose.
strengths.strength_expression: You're committing to the line — turn-in to apex on one input, with no mid-corner renegotiation.

events.coaching_expression: Let the fronts finish their work before you ask them to steer — trail the brake in, don't drop it.
events.drill: Next session: on medium-speed corners, deliberately delay full brake release ~0.2 s into the corner. Ignore lap time. Feel the car keep pointing at the apex.
events.driving_principle: Front tires can't both decelerate and steer at the limit. Releasing brake pressure well before turn-in unloads the front axle before it has finished slowing the car, so there's no grip left to rotate.
events.rationale: This lap: near_stop+spin at corner C14, min speed 21 km/h, peak yaw 0.98 rad/s. still braking (1.00) as the car snapped — the rear stepped out under trailing brake into the corner.

incidents.note: Incidents are single events (N=1): this lap did X, decomposable to the trace. Not a driver trait, and never priced as recoverable time. An 'unclassified' incident is detected but its cause was not clean enough to name — stated, not guessed.
